Switched off because the r1 restarted twice in a row soon after the tweaks went in. One of them is probably the reason. Switch this back on to try again.

Deep sleep hands the whole chip to the firmware, which switches off almost everything. Light sleep only freezes the apps and lets the cores idle.\n\nIf the r1 hangs or restarts in sleep, light sleep skips the firmware. It drains the battery a lot faster, so it\'s more of a test than a fix.
Switched off while the screen is off
Stay on while the screen is off
Switches processor cores off, the little ones first. The first core always stays on.\n\nIf the r1 gets steadier with fewer cores, one of them is flaky. Apps run slower.
The temperature the cores start slowing down at to cool off.\n\nLower keeps the r1 cooler in the hand. Higher keeps speeds up for longer, but the chip runs hotter; above 85 °C you\'re on your own.
How loud the speaker gets at full volume.\n\nMore is louder but distorts sooner on loud music; less keeps it clean and saves a little battery.
How much the mic amplifies, 24 dB being its most.\n\nLess keeps loud voices and music from clipping in recordings and calls.
How fast the camera turns.\n\nQuick opens the camera sooner but the motor may slip and land a little off; Gentle turns it slower and quieter.
Where the camera turns to while no app uses it.\n\nHidden keeps the sensor covered. Resting toward a side opens the camera that way at once.
The fastest the graphics chip runs.\n\nLower keeps the r1 cooler and the battery going longer in games and animations; the full speed keeps them smooth.
How the cores pick their speed.\n\nBalanced speeds up with the work. Performance keeps every core at its top speed, hot and hungry; Battery keeps them at the lowest, slow but frugal.
How readily idle memory goes to the compressed swap.\n\nLower keeps more in RAM, quicker to switch back to but sooner full. Higher compresses early, keeping more apps around at a little CPU cost.
How the storage orders its reads and writes.\n\nmq-deadline keeps reads quick under load, kyber aims for steady latency, none leaves the order to the eMMC itself.
How much the storage reads past what an app asks for.\n\nMore speeds up reading big files and starting apps, less wastes no memory on what isn\'t read.

Memory set aside to keep idle apps compressed instead of closing them.\n\nMore keeps more apps open in the background but takes RAM from the app in front. Changing it takes a moment while swapped out apps move back.

At the stock top voltage, faster only where this r1 passed the stress test. It runs warmer and the battery lasts less; the throttle temperatures still apply, so the extra speed mostly shows in short bursts. Kept when the r1 restarts; if it fails to start twice in a row, the tweaks switch themselves off.

Dots: green is safe to try, yellow is a last resort, red can stop things from working. Changes kick in right away and stay after a restart; two restarts in a row soon after they went in switch the tweaks off.
